summary: Bala Sahai Shastri worked in Indology at Panjab University, where he served as Assistant (attested 1932) and in-charge of the Sanskrit Section (attested 1947).

Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, Baladora Indrajothi earned degrees and a Hindi diploma from the University of Kelaniya and studied at Oriental Studies Society. Career posts include teacher at Vidyalankara Pirivena, Junior Fellow at Kelaniya, and lecturer at Bhiksu University.

A scholar of philosophy and Indology, Balaganapathi Devarakonda completed an M.A. at the University of Delhi (1993–1995) and a PhD at the University of Hyderabad (1997–2004). He was appointed Professor at the University of Delhi in 2015.

Baliram Shukla works in the fields of philosophy and Indology. His academic posts at Savitribai Phule Pune University include Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and Professor (attested 2026).
Active in Indology and linguistics, Balram Shukla studied at the University of Delhi from around 2002 to 2009. He served as a Professor at the University of Delhi in 2004.

Balthasar Bickel is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Zurich (~1986–1997). He held a post at the University of Leipzig (~2002–2011) and served on the editorial board at the University of Zurich (~2011).

Bangwei Wang specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, completing his doctoral dissertation at Peking University in 1987. His career at Peking University includes appointments as Professor (attested 2000–2007, 2017) and Boya Retired Professor (attested 2026).

A scholar of linguistics and Indology, Banikanta Kakati studied at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. He served as Professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and Dean and Department Head at Gauhati University in 1948.

Bapu Deva Sastri was an Indologist who studied at Sehore Sanskrit School under Lancelot Wilkinson and Sevarama, as well as under Dhundiraja Misra. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.

Barbara A. Holdrege works in religious studies and Indology. She has held posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara, including Associate Professor of the Comparative History of Religions (attested 2000) and Professor (attested 2026).

A scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, Barbara Ambros earned degrees from Columbia and Harvard. She held posts at Temple University Japan, Trinity College, Sophia, Wesleyan, ICU, and Columbia, becoming Professor at UNC Chapel Hill in 2015.

Barbara Catharina Jacoba Timmer specialized in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Leiden University and completed her Ph.D. at the University of Amsterdam in 1930, studying under Marcel Cohen, Barend Faddegon, and Jean Philippe Vogel.

Barbara Diane Miller worked in Tibetology. She earned a B.A. from the University of Michigan in 1948 and a Ph.D. from the University of Washington in 1958, later teaching at Beloit College and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

A scholar of Sinology, Barbara E. Ward earned degrees at Newnham College, Cambridge, the University of London, and LSE. She held teaching posts and fellowships at Cambridge, London, CUHK, and Cornell, and headed the IIED in 1973.

Tibetologist and religious studies scholar Barbara Gerke completed her D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held research posts at Berlin, Oxford, and CSDS, and joined the faculty at the University of Vienna (attested 2022–2026).

Specializing in Indology and development studies, Barbara Harriss-White studied at Newstead Wood School. She held posts at the University of East Anglia (~1979–1990), Queen Elizabeth House (~1990–2011), and Wolfson College, Oxford (~1990).

A scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology, Barbara Mittler studied at Pearson College, the Mandarin Training Center, the University of Oxford (~1987–1990), and Heidelberg University (~1990–1994), holding a post at Heidelberg in 1993.

Barbara Nimri Aziz specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a B.A. from Queen's University at Kingston and a Ph.D. in social anthropology from SOAS under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf, holding a post at the University of Oran in 2007.

Indologist Barbara Stoler Miller earned degrees from Barnard, Columbia, and Penn under W. Norman Brown, Royal W. Weiler, and Stella Kramrisch. She served as Professor at Barnard and Columbia (~1968–1993) and President of the Association for Asian Studies (1990).

Specializing in Indology and religious studies, Barbora Sojková earned degrees from Charles University, Wolfson College, Balliol College, and UCL. In 2025, she held postdoctoral researcher posts at the University of Oxford and the University of Zurich.
